html:
SMTO-SKL-0082 — The repeat settings for this meeting aren't complete

GUID: d4d58002-f705-51e1-a8a6-9d0ea3cfe246
Slug: microsoft365-invalid-recurrence
Domain: SKL · Subsystem: microsoft365

What happened

  • You asked for a repeating calendar event, but the repeat details don't fit together, such as no weekdays chosen or no clear end. SMTO stopped before contacting Microsoft, so no event was created or changed.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. For a weekly event, say which days it happens, for example “every Monday and Wednesday”. A weekly repeat can't be set up without its weekdays.
  2. Say either how many times it repeats (“for 10 weeks”) or the last date (“until March 31”), but not both. SMTO needs one clear end, and two different ends could disagree.
  3. Make sure the end date isn't before the first event, then ask SMTO to create or update the event again. An end date before the start can't produce any events.

What success looks like

  • The repeating event appears in your Outlook calendar on the days and dates you expected.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them, with how you described the repeat, to the person who manages SMTO. SMTO supports daily and weekly repeats only.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Microsoft 365 event_body rejected the recurrence: a weekly pattern had no days_of_week, count and until were both supplied or both missing, or until was not a valid date or fell before the first occurrence's date.

What this means

  • Weekly recurrence omits days, count and until are both present/absent, or the until date is invalid or before the start. This explanation performs no Microsoft request. The original operation stage and receipt determine its effect; keep the selected tenant, account and resource identity fixed during recovery.

Why this can happen

  • Weekly recurrence omits days, count and until are both present/absent, or the until date is invalid or before the start.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect frequency, days_of_week and exactly one valid ending.

How to fix it

  • Provide recurrence with frequency daily or weekly, an optional interval, exactly one of count or until (ISO date on or after the start date), and days_of_week for weekly patterns; then repeat calendar_create_event or calendar_update_event.
  • Use daily or weekly recurrence with exactly one of count or until; weekly recurrence also needs days_of_week.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect provider state and exact account authority first.

How to verify the fix

  • The intended series has a supported recurrence with an unambiguous end.

What not to do

  • Do not expose secrets or blindly replay uncertain mutations.

Technical notes

  • This explanation performs no Microsoft request. The original operation stage and receipt determine its effect; keep the selected tenant, account and resource identity fixed during recovery.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
